figures.caption: Fig. 1. Operando neutron imaging platform and custom all-solid-state cell. (a) Experimental configuration with a goniometer-mounted stage, collimated neutron beam, and high-resolution detector. (b) PTFE-based operando cell with stainless-steel plungers and ceramic insulators. (c) Representative neutron radiograph of the assembled cell. (d) Neutron transmission image. The grayscale represents the normalized neutron transmission. (e) Pseudo-color image used to visualize relative lithium redistribution with respect to the initial pristine stage. The color scale represents relative change for better visualization.

Fig. 2. Operando neutron radiography of the first charge–discharge cycle at 0.5 mA cm−2 for the Si|LPSCl|NMC811 cell. (a) Voltage profile with selected states. (b,c) Pseudo-color image maps during charge and discharge showing relative transmission ratio changes with respect to the initial/pristine stage. (d,e) Through-thickness line profiles obtained by averaging the neutron transmission along the thickness direction of the electrodes at different charge/discharge stages. (f) Through-thickness line profile comparison of pristine, fully charged, and fully discharged states highlighting first-cycle irreversibility.

Fig. 3. Rate-dependent operando neutron radiography of the Si|LPSCl|NMC811 cell. (a-d) Cycling at 0.5 mA cm−2. (e-h) Cycling at 1.0 mA cm−2. Pseudo-color image and line profiles compare how current density changes the reaction topology across the cathode thickness.

Fig. 4. Spatiotemporal maps of relative lithium change across the NMC811 cathode derived from operando neutron radiography. The in-plane transmission is averaged over the radial direction for the (a) Charge and (b) Discharge at 0.5 mA cm−2. The maps highlight a non-monotonic reaction sequence and a persistent interior reaction zone, highlighted by the lithium depletion contour lines. (c) Three-dimensional surface plots showing lithium concentration change (ΔCLi) as a function of electrode depth and time during charge (left) and discharge (right).

Fig. 5. Three-dimensional neutron tomography reconstructions after full discharge. (a-c) Representative orthogonal cross-sections of the silicon anode extracted from the reconstructed volume. (d-f) Representative orthogonal cross-sections of the NMC811 cathode extracted from the reconstructed volume.

Fig. 6. Cross-sectional Raman mapping of chemical evolution in the composite cathode. (a) Optical micrograph with the green box showing the mapped region. (b) Raman contour maps at selected states of charge. (c-g) Representative normalized spectra collected near the current collector, in the cathode center, and near the solid-electrolyte side. (h) Evolution of the average normalized 460/425 cm−1 Raman intensity ratio across the current collector side, center region, and solid electrolyte side of the thick cathode during charging.
Table 1 Raman shifts associated with LPSCl and the corresponding detectable species at each Raman shift.
